newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish resort bomber targeted police -- officials.
newsitem.headline: Turkish resort bomber targeted police -- officials.

text.p: A suspected Kurdish rebel who died in a botched grenade attack in a popular Turkish tourist resort was planning to strike at police targets, a local official said on Monday.

"Notes that were found lead us to the opinion that the terrorist woman's targets were police vehicles, stations and lodgings," local governor Cemil Serhadli said in a statement quoted by state-run Anatolian news agency.

The woman died on Saturday night in a public toilet in the southwestern Turkish town of Bodrum while trying to assemble makeshift time bombs with five grenades and watches. The other grenades did not explode.

Serhadli said a previous identification of the woman was found to be incorrect, but she was still thought to have been a member of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), fighting for Kurdish self-rule in the southeast.
No group has claimed responsibility for the bombing.
The PKK has attacked tourist resorts in the past in an effort to reduce Turkey's valuable income from tourism.
Serhadli said the blast had not caused panic among the tens of thousands of Turkish and foreign tourists in Bodrum, a whitewashed town on the Aegean Sea popular with British and German holidaymakers.
"People were out until four o'clock this morning at bars and discos enjoying themselves," he told Reuters by telephone.
